issues.display_title: Issue #462: Consolidate Post Follower Count Lookup
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 19/08/26

✅ Implementation: Consolidate Post Follower Count Lookup

Changes

  • Added PostFunctions.GetFollowerCount to own the repeated followers_counts query.
  • Preserved the legacy Scan into []map[string]interface{}, empty-result check, and int64 assertion.
  • Added a Posts-package getFollowerCount wrapper to centralize the shared Fiber 400 and 409 responses.
  • Added an explicit boolean stop signal because Functions.ErrorResponse can successfully write JSON and return nil.
  • Replaced five duplicated blocks:
    • Three in AddPost.
    • One in AddPostGothru.
    • One in DownloadUploadFileGDV1.
  • Left AddPostComplete and AddPostCompleteEmbed unchanged because they use scalar scanning and RowsAffected semantics.
  • Added focused tests for successful query-result extraction, query failure, missing rows, and HTTP response mapping.

Verification

go test ./src/Action/V1/Posts ./src/Utils/Functions/PostFunctions
go test ./...
go vet ./src/Action/V1/Posts ./src/Utils/Functions/PostFunctions
git diff --name-only -- src/Worker src/Action/V1/Cronjob
git diff --check

Results:

  • Focused Posts and PostFunctions tests pass.
  • Full repository tests pass.
  • Focused go vet passes.
  • No worker or cronjob file changed.
  • Diff whitespace validation passes; only Git line-ending warnings are reported.
  • Independent review found and verified the fix for the Fiber nil-error stop-signal edge case; final review has no blocking findings.
  • API smoke was unavailable because the local service on port 9999 was not running.

Git

  • Commit : eb93989
  • Pushed to origin/development.

Problem

Five post creation flows repeat the same followers_counts query, query-error response, missing-row response, and total_followers extraction. This duplicates DB and HTTP behavior across three handlers and makes future changes inconsistent.

Scope

  • Add a shared follower-count query helper in PostFunctions.
  • Add a Posts-package wrapper for the shared 400 and 409 Fiber responses.
  • Replace the five exact slice/map lookup blocks in AddPost, AddPostGothru, and DownloadUploadFileGDV1.
  • Preserve the existing query, response status codes, messages, and int64 assertion behavior.
  • Preserve the stop signal after Functions.ErrorResponse, which writes the response and can return nil.
  • Leave the two scalar RowsAffected variants in AddPostComplete and AddPostCompleteEmbed unchanged.
  • Do not change worker or cronjob code.

Acceptance Criteria

  • All five exact lookup blocks call the shared helper.
  • Query failure still returns HTTP 400 with Check Follower Failed.
  • Missing follower count still returns HTTP 409 with Follower Count Not Found.
  • Successful lookup returns the existing int64 follower count for score calculation.
  • Callers stop after either error response even when Fiber returns a nil Go error.
  • Focused tests, go test ./..., and go vet succeed.
  • No worker or cronjob file changes.
  • git diff --check succeeds.

Delivery

  • Implemented locally on development.
  • Not committed or pushed.

RESULT 19/08/26

✅ Implementation: Consolidate JPEG Filename Generation

Changes

  • Added Functions.GenerateJPEGFilename, returning the complete JPEG filename, its random basename, and an error.
  • Kept time.Now() inside the public helper so every invocation reads the current runtime clock using the server or container local timezone, matching the previous behavior.
  • Kept the existing three-byte RandomHex input, producing six lowercase hexadecimal characters.
  • Replaced ten duplicated blocks across seven consumer files:
    • Four in AddPost.
    • One in AddPostGothru.
    • One in DownloadUploadFileGDV1.
    • One in UploadPanoramaDbx.
    • One in UploadPanoramaGDrive.
    • One in UploadPanoramaPost.
    • One in PostFunctions.ProcessThumbnail.
  • Preserved basename usage in Dropbox, Google Drive, and direct panorama upload responses.
  • Preserved each caller's existing random-generation error message.
  • Removed imports that became unused after consolidation.
  • Left avatar, profile, collection thumbnail, cover, attachment, register, worker, and cronjob filename flows outside the approved scope.

Tests

  • Added a runtime-format test for timestamp, random hexadecimal component, basename, and .jpg extension.
  • Added a deterministic timestamp-format test.
  • Added a random-generation error propagation test.

Verification

go test ./...

git diff --check

  • Full repository tests pass.
  • Focused go vet passes.
  • All ten approved duplicate blocks use the shared helper.
  • No worker or cronjob file changed.
  • Diff whitespace validation passes; only Git line-ending warnings are reported.
  • Independent review reports no findings.
  • API smoke was unavailable because the local service on port 9999 was not running.

  • Commit : c755f52
  • Pushed to origin/development.

Problem

Ten post and panorama flows repeat the same JPEG filename generation logic: a runtime timestamp formatted as YYYYMMDDHHMMSS, three random bytes encoded as six lowercase hexadecimal characters, and the .jpg extension.

Scope

  • Add a shared JPEG filename generator in the Functions package.
  • Return both the complete filename and random basename because three API responses still expose the basename.
  • Replace ten matching blocks across seven post and panorama consumer files.
  • Preserve runtime time.Now() behavior, server-local timezone, random-byte length, lowercase hexadecimal encoding, and .jpg extension.
  • Preserve caller-specific error responses and messages.
  • Leave filename patterns with variable extensions or different naming rules unchanged.
  • Do not change worker or cronjob code.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Each generated filename matches YYYYMMDDHHMMSS.<6 lowercase hex characters>.jpg.
  • The timestamp is evaluated whenever GenerateJPEGFilename is called, not during application build or package initialization.
  • The returned basename matches the six-character random component in the filename.
  • Random generation errors are returned to callers without changing their existing HTTP response mapping.
  • All ten scoped duplicate blocks use the shared helper.
  • Focused tests, go test ./..., and go vet succeed.
  • No worker or cronjob file changes.
  • git diff --check succeeds.

Delivery

  • Implemented locally on development.
  • Not committed or pushed.

RESULT 20/08/26

✅ Implementation: Consolidate Post Description Validation

Changes

  • Added PostFunctions.ValidateAndEscapeDescription beside other post-domain helpers in PostsFunctions.go.
  • The helper:
    • Rejects empty or whitespace-only descriptions.
    • Counts Unicode runes and enforces the existing 2,200-rune maximum.
    • Escapes accepted descriptions with html.EscapeString.
    • Returns an explicit boolean stop signal for Fiber response handling.
  • Replaced eight duplicated blocks:
    • Three in AddPost.
    • One in AddPostGothru.
    • One publish branch in AddPostComplete.
    • One in AddPostCompleteEmbed.
    • One in EditPostDescription.
    • One in UpdatePostVideo.
  • Preserved guarded and direct type-assertion behavior in AddPost.
  • Left the optional draft branch in AddPostComplete unchanged; it still escapes only non-empty descriptions and does not add the publish maximum validation.
  • Removed validation imports that became unused in action files.
  • Kept controller, profile, affiliate, optional-only escape, worker, and cronjob flows outside scope because their semantics differ.

Tests

  • Added PostFunctions tests covering:
    • HTML escaping.
    • The exact 2,200-Unicode-rune boundary.
    • Rejection at 2,201 Unicode runes.
    • Whitespace-only rejection.
    • Exact description-required and description-max response input codes.

Verification

go test ./...

git diff --check

Results:

  • Focused helper and Posts package tests pass.
  • Full repository tests pass.
  • Focused go vet passes.
  • No import cycle was introduced.
  • All eight scoped blocks use the PostFunctions helper.
  • Optional draft behavior remains unchanged.
  • No worker or cronjob file changed.
  • Diff whitespace validation passes; only Git line-ending warnings are reported.
  • Independent reviews report no findings before and after moving the helper into PostFunctions.

  • Commit : 7d6bad6
  • Pushed to origin/development.

Problem

Eight post flows repeat the same required-description validation, 2,200-rune limit, HTTP error responses, and HTML escaping. Keeping this logic in each handler risks inconsistent validation and escaping behavior.

Scope

  • Add a shared ValidateAndEscapeDescription helper in PostFunctions.
  • Replace eight matching required-description blocks across six Posts action files.
  • Preserve validation order: required check after trimming, length check on the original value, then HTML escaping.
  • Preserve the exact HTTP 400 messages and input codes.
  • Preserve the explicit boolean stop signal because Functions.ErrorResponse can write a response and return a nil Go error.
  • Keep the optional draft-description behavior in AddPostComplete unchanged.
  • Leave validation flows with different limits, optional-only escaping, logging, or response behavior unchanged.
  • Do not change worker or cronjob code.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Empty and whitespace-only required descriptions return description-required.
  • Descriptions containing at most 2,200 Unicode runes are accepted.
  • Descriptions containing more than 2,200 Unicode runes return description-max.
  • Accepted descriptions are escaped with html.EscapeString after validation.
  • Original whitespace is preserved in accepted stored values.
  • All eight matching blocks call PostFunctions.ValidateAndEscapeDescription.
  • Optional draft descriptions retain their previous behavior.
  • Focused tests, go test ./..., and go vet succeed.
  • No worker or cronjob file changes.
  • git diff --check succeeds.

Delivery

  • Implemented locally on development.
  • Not committed or pushed.

RESULT 20/08/26

✅ Implementation: Consolidate Numeric-Only Username Detection

Changes

  • Added Functions.IsNumericString in Functions.go.
  • The helper delegates to strconv.Atoi and returns whether conversion succeeded, preserving the previous behavior exactly.
  • Replaced seven duplicated checks:
    • One in V1 Users/EditProfile.
    • One in V2 Users/EditProfile.
    • One in RegisterUser.
    • One in RegisterGoogle.
    • One in RegisterApple.
    • Two in ValidateRegister.
  • Preserved caller-specific behavior:
    • Edit and standard-register flows still reject numeric-only usernames with their existing responses.
    • Google, Apple, and generated-username flows still append "a".
  • Removed unused strconv imports from both EditProfile files and ValidateRegister; retained imports still used for OTP or username suffix conversion.
  • Kept worker, cronjob, and API collection files outside scope.

Tests

  • Added a table-driven helper test covering:
    • Digits.
    • Positive and negative signs.
    • Empty input.
    • Alphanumeric input.
    • Leading whitespace.
    • Integer overflow.
  • Verified the test failed with undefined: IsNumericString before adding the helper, then passed after implementation.

Problem

Seven username flows repeat the same strconv.Atoi check to detect numeric-only usernames. Keeping the detection logic in each handler risks inconsistent behavior when the validation changes.

Scope

  • Add a shared Functions.IsNumericString helper.
  • Replace seven matching checks across six Register and Users action files.
  • Preserve the exact strconv.Atoi semantics, including signed values, whitespace handling, and integer overflow behavior.

issues.display_title: Issue #466: Consolidate Forbidden Email Character Validation
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 20/08/26

✅ Implementation: Consolidate Forbidden Email Character Validation

Changes

  • Added a package-level precompiled forbiddenEmailCharacters regex in RegistrationFunctions.go.
  • Added RegisterFunctions.HasForbiddenEmailCharacters, which evaluates values against the exact legacy blacklist.
  • Replaced five duplicated per-request regex compilation and matching blocks:
    • RegisterUser.
    • RegisterGoogle.
    • ValidateRegister.
    • ForgotPassword.
    • ResendOtp.
  • Preserved each caller's existing HTTP response, message, input code, and continuation behavior.
  • Preserved mail.ParseAddress checks and their original position after forbidden-character validation.
  • Removed only regex imports that became unused; retained regex imports needed by other validations.
  • Left the different no-space character class used by profile and Street View fields outside scope.
  • Kept worker, cronjob, and API collection files outside scope.

Tests

  • Added a table-driven test covering:
    • Space rejection.
    • Plus-sign rejection.
    • Backtick rejection.
    • Acceptance of @ and ..
    • Acceptance of -.
    • Empty input.
  • Verified the test first failed with undefined: HasForbiddenEmailCharacters, then passed after implementation.

Verification

go test ./src/Utils/Functions/Registration -run TestHasForbiddenEmailCharacters -count=1
go test ./src/Action/V1/Register ./src/Action/V1/Users ./src/Utils/Functions/Registration -count=1
go test ./... -count=1
go vet ./src/Action/V1/Register ./src/Action/V1/Users ./src/Utils/Functions/Registration
git diff --name-only -- src/Worker src/Action/V1/Cronjob
git diff --check

Results:

  • Focused helper and affected-package tests pass.
  • Full repository tests pass.
  • Focused go vet passes.
  • All five scoped blocks use the shared predicate.
  • No worker or cronjob file changed.
  • Diff whitespace validation passes; only Git line-ending warnings are reported.
  • Independent review reports no findings.

Git

  • Commit : 5c37006
  • Pushed to origin/development.

Problem

Five registration and user flows compile and evaluate the same forbidden-character regex on every request. Duplicating the predicate risks inconsistent accepted characters and unnecessary repeated regex compilation.

Scope

  • Add a shared RegisterFunctions.HasForbiddenEmailCharacters predicate.
  • Precompile the existing forbidden-character regex once at package initialization.
  • Replace five identical validation blocks in Register and Users actions.
  • Preserve the exact blacklist, including rejection of spaces and plus signs while allowing @, ., and -.
  • Preserve caller-specific HTTP statuses, messages, input codes, and validation order.
  • Keep mail.ParseAddress checks unchanged because they validate different email rules.
  • Leave the no-space forbidden-character variants used by profile and Street View fields unchanged.
  • Do not change worker or cronjob code.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Spaces, plus signs, backticks, and every character in the legacy blacklist are rejected.
  • @, ., and - remain accepted by this predicate.
  • Empty input remains accepted by this predicate and continues to be handled by existing required-field validation.
  • All five matching action blocks call RegisterFunctions.HasForbiddenEmailCharacters.
  • Existing response status, message, code, and mail.ParseAddress ordering remain unchanged.
  • Focused tests, go test ./..., and focused go vet succeed.
  • No worker or cronjob file changes.
  • git diff --check succeeds.

Delivery

  • Implemented locally on development.
  • Not committed or pushed.
